consensus_summary: All four blind responses identify dew primarily as divine blessing, favor, and life-giving refreshment/grace descending quietly on God's people (Gen 27:28; Deut 33:13,28; Hos 14:5; Ps 133:3), with well-attested secondary senses: God's word or teaching (Deut 32:2, listed as a common alternative), transience (Hos 6:4; 13:3), resurrection (Isa 26:19), provision via manna, and pneumatological/Marian readings.
book_summary: The book identifies dew as the word of God descending from heaven — silent, nightly, found in the morning (Deut 32:2). It ties the dew to the manna (Num 11:9; Ex 16:14) read through Deut 8:3 (man lives by every word from the LORD's mouth), so the word lies on the ground as daily bread; it also folds the transience motif into this reading (word received without root evaporates), and explicitly notes the common view (blessing/refreshment/Spirit) as distinct from its own.
consensus_core_identification: Dew = God's blessing, favor, and refreshing, life-giving grace upon His people.
book_core_identification: Dew = the word of God, descending silently from heaven and received as daily nourishment (with the manna as its embodiment).
boundary_disagreement: The book pulls the manna passages (Ex 16:14; Num 11:9), which the consensus files under providential provision/blessing, into the word category via Deut 8:3; it also reclassifies the transience motif (consensus: a separate negative sense about fleeting devotion) as the word evaporating when received without root, and reads even Hos 14:5 within the word-frame rather than as generic blessing.
material_contradiction: The consensus's central referent is divine blessing/grace itself; the book replaces this with a specific referent — the word of God — and explicitly flags the blessing/refreshment/Spirit reading as merely 'commonly taught,' i.e., not its own identification. As the single primary identification of what dew symbolizes, 'blessing/favor' and 'the descending word' cannot both hold; the book elevates what the consensus treats as a secondary alternative into a replacement of the primary sense.
rationale: This is not a mere boundary adjustment: the book does not keep 'blessing' as the category and narrow it; it substitutes a different central referent (the word), organizing the whole entry — including the manna and the transience motif — around it. The word-as-dew reading appears in the consensus only as a listed 'common' alternative resting on Deut 32:2, so the book's core is recognizable but displaces the consensus primary, which fits DIVERGENT rather than REFINED (referent replaced) or NOVEL (the reading is attested among alternatives).
strongest_objection: One could argue REFINED: the word gently nourishing God's people is arguably a species of the consensus's broad 'blessing/refreshment' category, and every consensus response already lists Deut 32:2's word/doctrine sense as a common alternative — so the book merely re-weights an acknowledged sense rather than contradicting the consensus referent.
